problems.quote: Based on permutation tests with 10,000 iterations to compare average within-group idea similarity, the difference between idea groups is significant
problems.note: The paper reports permutation tests, confidence intervals and p-values, but does not specify the permutation unit or whether similarities sharing a participant were treated as independent. The extraction-spec se_basis definition and codebook Section 10 use 'pair' for uncertainty that treats pairs as independent observations. A pairwise outcome metric does not establish that uncertainty basis. The extraction's own qualification that the resampling unit is unspecified does not support a definite 'pair' code. No replacement basis can be confirmed from the PDF; retain this as unresolved/null rather than guessing. 'not_reported' would also be misleading here because contrast uncertainty is printed. This finding does not change the recorded numeric results or the pair unit of the similarity measure.

summary: Read the complete markdown conversion, including Appendices A-E and references, and checked all 14 estimates against the PDF. Every recorded numerical statistic and participant count is supported and belongs to the stated study, outcome and arms. All 42 estimate source quotes match their cited pages after removing PDF formatting artifacts. All nine supplied mechanical quote flags are false positives: the Study 1 similarity quote on PDF p. 8 splits 'difference' with a soft hyphen (U+00AD) and a line break; the eight Appendix D quotes on PDF p. 18 contain zero-width table padding (U+200B) between the assisted and human-only rows. Direct PDF text and table extraction confirm all Appendix D cells and the Study 1/Study 2 column assignments. Two problems remain: the pair uncertainty basis is asserted without sufficient reporting for the two similarity permutation analyses. The other requested outcome, design, direction, timing, measure and unit codes are supported. No additional identifiable in-scope full-sample outcome or contrast was found. The unquantified shorter-ideas statement on PDF p. 19 lacks a study attribution and a defined scored analysis and is already documented in not_extracted. Model-only stimulus comparisons, manipulation checks, subgroup analyses and distributional diagnostics are properly excluded.
